references.text: Abraham offers the three guests water to wash their feet and food to eat—a direct parallel to the hospitality shown to Abraham’s servant.
Lot invites the two angels into his house, offering foot washing and lodging—the same kind of hospitality that Laban shows.
Joseph receives his brothers in Egypt by giving them water to wash their feet and fodder for their donkeys—a close parallel to the hospitality shown in this verse.
An old man in Gibea takes in a traveler, gives fodder for the donkey and washes his feet—the same acts of hospitality as here.
Jesus points out that the host did not give him water to wash his feet, showing that foot washing was a basic act of hospitality.
Foot washing is mentioned as a good deed linked to hospitality, reflecting the biblical tradition of washing guests’ feet.
The call to show hospitality, for through this some have unknowingly entertained angels—underscores the value of the hospitality shown here.
